intro: A director or a ministry won't read 40 pages: they read the first page and decide. In this lesson you structure a proposal under clear headings, write an executive summary and recommendations a busy reader can act on, and cut the filler that makes business English long and heavy.
teachingNotes: Chain recap in one line each, don't re-teach: b2-formal-writing (formal register: no contractions, the passive where the doer isn't important, formal words and linkers; formal letters; a short report with Introduction / Findings / Recommendations, 'The aim of this report is to …', and 'It is recommended that …' taught there as a phrase to remember with plural subjects) and c1-nominalisation (verbs and adjectives → nouns, noun + preposition, complex noun phrases, and its warning: don't overdo it, because nouns can hide who did what). The learner has also met the parts of a long report (executive summary, background, method, findings, recommendations) as a READER in b2-reading-strategies and c1-reading-complex; here they WRITE them. New here: the proposal as a document type (it asks for approval or money for FUTURE work; a report says what happened or what was found), the six proposal headings, the executive summary, recommendations people can act on, and concise business style. Explain terms the first time in plain Indonesian: proposal (usulan kegiatan / proposal dana), report (laporan), heading (judul bagian), executive summary (ringkasan eksekutif: seluruh dokumen dalam satu halaman), filler (kata pengisi), BLUF (bottom line up front = intinya di depan).

Objective proposal-structure. Headings in this order (wording varies, and many ministries and donors give their own template: tell the learner to follow it): Background (the problem or opportunity NOW, with a few facts and numbers: why this is needed), Objectives (what the project will achieve, specific and measurable, usually 'To + verb' with who, how many and by when: To train 2,000 small business owners in Bandung by June 2027; 'To improve digital literacy' is too vague), Plan (also Approach, Methodology or Activities: what will be done and how), Budget (costs item by item with a total), Timeline (when: phases, months, deadlines, often a table), Expected results / Benefits (what will change, for whom, and how it will be measured). Long proposals start with an executive summary; some add Risks, Evaluation or About us. Headings are short nouns. Money: English writes Rp1,200,000,000 or Rp1.2 billion (or IDR 1.2 billion): commas for thousands, a point for decimals, the opposite of Indonesian Rp1.200.000.000 / Rp1,2 miliar; miliar = billion, juta = million. Test only sentences that clearly belong to one section (a problem with facts → Background; a cost → Budget; dates and phases → Timeline; activities and how → Plan). Objectives and Expected results can overlap: don't test that difference.

Indonesian proposal and report habits, named kindly (they are polite in Indonesian, just not the convention in English business writing): a long formulaic opening (Kata Pengantar, Puji syukur kehadirat Tuhan Yang Maha Esa …, Laporan ini disusun dalam rangka …) → leave it out and start with the purpose; a Background that starts with history or general truths (Indonesia adalah negara kepulauan …, Sejak zaman dahulu …, Di era globalisasi ini … → 'In this era of globalisation') → start with today's problem and a number; the campus template (BAB I Pendahuluan, Rumusan Masalah, Maksud dan Tujuan) → the English headings; the ending 'Demikian proposal ini kami sampaikan. Atas perhatian dan kerja samanya kami ucapkan terima kasih.' → end with the next step or the decision needed (We request approval by 30 November. / We would welcome the opportunity to discuss this proposal.); very long sentences joined with yang, dan, sehingga, serta, dalam rangka → one idea per sentence; word-for-word fillers: dalam rangka → 'in the framework of' (→ to / for), perlu diketahui bahwa → 'it needs to be known that' (→ delete).

Objective executive-summary. Written LAST (when the findings are known), read FIRST and often alone, one page or less, for a busy reader who decides (the director reads only this). It gives: the purpose (what the document is about or asks for), the key findings (2–3 facts with numbers), the recommendations, and the decision needed (what, by when, at what cost). BLUF: the main point in the first sentence (This report finds that … and recommends …; This proposal requests Rp1.2 billion to …). It is not an introduction or a table of contents ('This report consists of five chapters' ✗) and has nothing that isn't in the document. Recommendations: clear (one action each), actionable (who does what, by when), prioritised (numbered, most important first), linked to the findings ('Based on Finding 2, …': 'Based on' is a fixed phrase = berdasarkan). Patterns: We recommend + -ing (We recommend adding an evening shift); We recommend that + we / a plural subject + verb; X should + verb; It is recommended that … (B2 phrase); in a numbered list the plain verb (1. Add an evening sorting shift.). The classic error from 'merekomendasikan untuk': 'We recommend to hire …' ✗ → We recommend hiring …; the same with suggest (suggest moving, not 'suggest to move'); propose takes both (We propose to open … / We propose opening …). 'that + singular subject + base verb' (that the company hire) is the subjunctive of c1-subjunctive-formal: if the learner writes it, accept it and say it comes in that lesson; 'that the company should hire' (British) is always safe. Vague recommendations ('Delivery should be improved', 'More attention should be given') → ask: who does what, by when?

Objective concise-business-writing. Cut filler and wordy phrases: in order to → to; due to the fact that → because; at this point in time → now; make a decision regarding / about → decide on / about; a large number of → many; it should be noted that → delete; with regard to → about; prior to → before; in the event that → if; has the ability to → can; conduct a review of → review; give consideration to → consider. The node's common error: 'In order to be able to make a decision regarding the matter of the budget …' → 'To decide on the budget …'. Be honest: these are not grammar mistakes, just longer than needed, and 'in order to' is still useful (in order not to miss the deadline). Active over passive when the actor matters (who is responsible or who must act: 'Mistakes were made' → 'The night team sent 300 parcels to the wrong route'); the passive stays right when the doer is unknown or unimportant (b2-formal-writing). One idea per sentence (about 15–25 words). Front-load the point in emails and paragraphs too. Balance with c1-nominalisation: noun phrases are good in titles, headings and compact summaries (a 20% fall in late deliveries), but noun-heavy phrases that hide the action (make a decision regarding, conduct a review of, give consideration to) should become verbs. Concise is not telegraphic or rude: keep full, polite sentences. Grade free rewrites on meaning and concision, not one wording; praise first, then cut ONE more thing.

Limits: all A0–B2 grammar plus the chain (nominalisation, noun phrases). Keep other C1 structures out of examples: no inversion ('Should you have any questions' only as a phrase to remember), no cleft sentences, no subjunctive after recommend / suggest with a singular subject, no impersonal passives beyond the fixed phrases 'It is recommended that …' (B2) and 'It should be noted that …' (shown here only as filler to delete), no advanced participle clauses ('Based on …' is a fixed phrase). Don't teach hedging (c1-hedging), cohesion devices in depth (c1-cohesion) or SMART-goal theory. All organisations, people and numbers are invented practice examples, not real data. Contexts: Bu Ani's NGO in Bandung writing a proposal to a ministry for a digital literacy programme for small businesses; Budi's report on late deliveries for an e-commerce company in Surabaya; budgets in rupiah.

keyPoints.title: A proposal under six headings
keyPoints.explanation: A proposal asks a reader (a manager, a ministry, a donor) to approve and pay for future work; a report says what happened or what was found. Write a proposal under short headings: Background (the problem or opportunity now, with facts), Objectives (specific and measurable: To train 2,000 small business owners by June 2027), Plan (what you will do and how), Budget (costs item by item, with a total), Timeline (when: phases and dates) and Expected results (what will change, and how you will measure it). Start with today's problem, not with history or 'Puji syukur', and end with the next step, not 'Demikian proposal ini …'. In English budgets, commas mark thousands and a point marks decimals: Rp1,200,000,000 = Rp1.2 billion.

examples.en: Background: Only 2 in 10 small food businesses in Bandung accept digital payments.
examples.id: Latar belakang: Hanya 2 dari 10 usaha makanan kecil di Bandung yang menerima pembayaran digital.

examples.en: Objectives: To train 2,000 small business owners in Bandung to accept QRIS payments safely by June 2027.
examples.id: Tujuan: Melatih 2.000 pemilik usaha kecil di Bandung agar bisa menerima pembayaran QRIS dengan aman paling lambat Juni 2027.

examples.en: Budget: The total cost of the programme is Rp1.2 billion.
examples.id: Anggaran: Total biaya program ini Rp1,2 miliar.

id.title: Proposal dengan enam judul bagian
id.explanation: Proposal meminta pembaca (manajer, kementerian, donor) menyetujui dan membiayai pekerjaan di masa depan; laporan menceritakan apa yang sudah terjadi atau apa yang ditemukan. Tulis proposal dengan judul bagian yang pendek: Background (masalah atau peluang saat ini, dengan fakta), Objectives (spesifik dan terukur: To train 2,000 small business owners by June 2027), Plan (apa yang akan dilakukan dan bagaimana), Budget (biaya per item, dengan total), Timeline (kapan: tahap dan tanggal) dan Expected results (apa yang akan berubah, dan bagaimana mengukurnya). Mulai dengan masalah hari ini, bukan dengan sejarah atau 'Puji syukur', dan akhiri dengan langkah berikutnya, bukan 'Demikian proposal ini …'. Di anggaran berbahasa Inggris, koma menandai ribuan dan titik menandai desimal: Rp1,200,000,000 = Rp1.2 billion.

keyPoints.title: Executive summary and recommendations
keyPoints.explanation: An executive summary is written last but read first: one page or less for a busy reader, such as a director who reads nothing else. Put the bottom line up front (BLUF): the main point in the first sentence, then the key findings, the recommendations and the decision you need (what, by when, at what cost). Recommendations are clear, actionable (who does what, by when), numbered in order of priority and linked to the findings. Use We recommend + -ing, We recommend that + we / a plural subject + verb, or should + verb, not 'We recommend to …'.

examples.en: This report finds that most late deliveries in Surabaya begin at the warehouse, and recommends three changes.
examples.id: Laporan ini menemukan bahwa sebagian besar keterlambatan pengiriman di Surabaya berawal di gudang, dan merekomendasikan tiga perubahan.

examples.en: We recommend adding an evening sorting shift at the Rungkut warehouse.
examples.id: Kami merekomendasikan penambahan shift sortir malam di gudang Rungkut.

examples.en: We ask the board to approve Rp450 million by 30 November.
examples.id: Kami meminta direksi menyetujui Rp450 juta paling lambat 30 November.

id.title: Executive summary dan rekomendasi
id.explanation: Executive summary ditulis paling akhir tapi dibaca paling awal: satu halaman atau kurang, untuk pembaca yang sibuk, misalnya direktur yang tidak membaca bagian lain. Taruh intinya di depan (BLUF, bottom line up front): poin utama di kalimat pertama, lalu temuan utama, rekomendasi, dan keputusan yang kamu minta (apa, kapan, berapa biayanya). Rekomendasi harus jelas, bisa langsung dijalankan (siapa melakukan apa, kapan), diberi nomor sesuai prioritas, dan terhubung dengan temuan. Pakai We recommend + -ing, We recommend that + we / subjek jamak + kata kerja, atau should + kata kerja, bukan 'We recommend to …'.

keyPoints.title: Concise business writing
keyPoints.explanation: Cut filler and wordy phrases: in order to → to, due to the fact that → because, at this point in time → now, make a decision regarding → decide on, a large number of → many, and delete 'It should be noted that'. Use the active when it matters who acts, write one idea per sentence and put the main point first. Noun phrases are fine in titles and summaries, but don't hide the verb (make a decision → decide). Concise is not rude or telegraphic: keep full, polite sentences.

examples.en: In order to be able to make a decision regarding the matter of the budget, … → To decide on the budget, …
examples.id: Agar dapat mengambil keputusan mengenai masalah anggaran, … → Untuk memutuskan anggaran, …

examples.en: A decision was made to close the Gresik depot. → The operations director decided to close the Gresik depot.
examples.id: Telah diputuskan untuk menutup depo Gresik. → Direktur operasional memutuskan untuk menutup depo Gresik.

id.title: Menulis bisnis secara ringkas
id.explanation: Buang kata pengisi dan frasa bertele-tele: in order to → to, due to the fact that → because, at this point in time → now, make a decision regarding → decide on, a large number of → many, dan hapus 'It should be noted that'. Pakai kalimat aktif kalau penting siapa pelakunya, tulis satu ide per kalimat, dan taruh poin utama di depan. Frasa kata benda boleh di judul dan ringkasan, tapi jangan sembunyikan kata kerjanya (make a decision → decide). Ringkas bukan berarti kasar atau seperti telegram: tetap pakai kalimat lengkap dan sopan.

guidedPractice.prompt: Bu Ani's proposal has six headings: Background, Objectives, Plan, Budget, Timeline, Expected results. Under which heading does this line go? 'Venue hire: 40 workshops × Rp6,000,000 = Rp240,000,000'
guidedPractice.hint: It's a cost, item by item: the section with the money.

guidedPractice.prompt: Which is the better objective for the proposal? Write a or b. (a) To improve digital literacy in Bandung. (b) To train 2,000 small business owners in Bandung to accept QRIS payments safely by June 2027.
guidedPractice.hint: A good objective is specific and measurable: who, how many, what and by when. Which one can you check at the end of the project?

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one word: An executive summary is written ___, but it is read first.
guidedPractice.hint: You can only summarise the findings and recommendations when you know them.

guidedPractice.prompt: Correct the mistake in this recommendation: 'We recommend to train all drivers to use the new app before December.'
expected: we recommend training all drivers to use the new app before december
we recommend that we train all drivers to use the new app before december
we recommend that all drivers are trained to use the new app before december
guidedPractice.hint: After recommend, use -ing or that + subject + verb, not to + verb (a word-for-word 'merekomendasikan untuk').

guidedPractice.prompt: Make it concise: replace 'at this point in time' with one word. 'At this point in time, the Rungkut warehouse has 45 staff.'

independentPractice.prompt: Write the first sentence of the executive summary for Bu Ani's proposal to the ministry. Put the bottom line up front: what the NGO asks for, how much, and what it will achieve.
expected: this proposal requests rp1.2 billion to train 2,000 small business owners in bandung to accept digital payments safely by june 2027
we request rp1.2 billion to train 2,000 small business owners in bandung to use qris safely by june 2027
independentPractice.hint: Rubric: one sentence with the request (requests / asks for), the amount in rupiah (Rp1.2 billion, written the English way) and the result (who, how many, by when). No thanks, no history, no 'This proposal consists of …'. Many wordings are fine: judge whether a director would know the point after one sentence.

independentPractice.prompt: Rewrite this as two short, clear sentences in the active: 'With regard to the problem of late deliveries in East Surabaya, which has been experienced by a large number of customers since August, a decision was made by the operations team to conduct a review of all the routes.'
expected: since august many customers in east surabaya have received late deliveries. the operations team decided to review all the routes
many customers in east surabaya have had late deliveries since august. the operations team has decided to review all the routes
independentPractice.hint: Rubric: cut 'with regard to' and 'a large number of' (→ many), make the team the subject (the operations team decided / has decided), turn 'conduct a review of' into the verb 'review', and split it into two sentences. Keep all the facts: East Surabaya, since August, all the routes.

independentPractice.prompt: Bu Ani's first draft of the Background starts: 'Indonesia is an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands, and in this era of globalisation, technology is very important.' Write a better first sentence that starts with today's problem.
expected: many small food businesses in bandung still accept only cash because they do not trust digital payments
last year many small traders in bandung lost money to fake payment links
independentPractice.hint: Rubric: start with the current problem in Bandung and, ideally, a number (how many businesses, how much money lost). No history, no general truths about Indonesia or globalisation. Any clear, factual problem sentence is fine; the numbers are invented.

assessment.prompt: Bu Ani's proposal to the ministry has six headings: Background, Objectives, Plan, Budget, Timeline, Expected results. Under which heading do these lines go? Write the heading. 'Trainer recruitment: November–December 2026. Workshops: January–June 2027. Final evaluation: by the end of September 2027.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: Timeline (phases with months and a deadline: WHEN things happen). 'Plan' = no credit: the Plan says what will be done and how, the Timeline says when. 'Schedule' = mostly correct (the right idea, but the heading in the list is Timeline).

assessment.prompt: Same proposal, same six headings: Background, Objectives, Plan, Budget, Timeline, Expected results. Under which heading does this sentence go? Write the heading. 'Each three-hour workshop will have three parts: setting up QRIS, spotting fake payment links, and practice on the participants' own phones.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: Plan (the activities: what will be done and how). Approach, Methodology or Activities = full credit (other names for the same section). 'Objectives' = no credit: objectives say what the project will achieve (To train 2,000 owners by June 2027), not what happens in each workshop. 'Timeline' = no credit: there are no dates.

assessment.prompt: Budi's executive summary for the director has four parts: Purpose, Key findings, Recommendations, Decision needed. Which part does this sentence belong to? Write its name. 'Seven in ten complaints in the third quarter came from customers who did not know where their parcel was.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: Key findings (a fact with a number that Budi's research found). 'Recommendations' = no credit: the sentence says what IS, not what should be done. 'Purpose' or 'Decision needed' = no credit.

assessment.prompt: Complete Budi's recommendation with one verb: 'Based on Finding 3, we ___ sending customers an automatic WhatsApp message when a parcel is late.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: recommend (suggest, propose or advise are also correct: all can be followed by -ing). 'recommended' = half credit (a recommendation is about what should happen now, so use the present). 'recommendation' = no credit (a noun, not a verb). 'consider' = half credit (it means 'think about', not a recommendation). 'want', 'need' or 'should' = no credit (they don't fit before -ing here).

assessment.prompt: Make this sentence from Budi's report more concise: replace 'due to the fact that' with one word. 'Many drivers missed their delivery slots due to the fact that the road to the warehouse was flooded.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: because (as or since are also fine). 'because of' or 'due to' = half credit: they need a noun after them (because of the flood), but here a full clause follows (the road … was flooded).

assessment.prompt: Make this sentence more concise: replace 'make a decision regarding' with two words. 'The board will make a decision regarding the new warehouse on Friday.'
assessment.rubric: Correct: decide on (decide about is also fine). 'decide' alone = half credit: 'decide the new warehouse' needs on or about. 'make decision' or 'decision on' = no credit (still a noun, not the verb).

assessment.prompt: Cut the filler phrase and write the whole sentence concisely: 'It should be noted that complaints about late parcels fell sharply in October.'
acceptableAnswers: complaints about late parcels fell sharply in october
in october complaints about late parcels fell sharply
complaints about late parcels dropped sharply in october
assessment.rubric: Correct: Complaints about late parcels fell sharply in October. ('It should be noted that' adds words but no meaning: the fact is the point.) Keeping a shorter filler ('Note that …', 'Notably, …') = half credit. Losing information (no 'sharply' or no 'in October') = half credit.

blocks.text:
Quick recap: in B2 you wrote formal letters and a short **report** (*Introduction, Findings, Recommendations*), and in the last lesson you packed ideas into noun phrases (*a sharp rise in online sales*). Now the bigger documents of working life.

A **proposal** asks a reader, such as a manager, a ministry or a donor, to **approve and pay for future work**. A **report** tells the reader what happened or what was found. Both use **headings** (a short name above each part), so a busy reader can jump to the part they need.

A proposal usually has these six headings (organisations name them a little differently, and many ministries and donors give you their own template: follow it):
- **Background**: the problem or opportunity **now**, with a few facts and numbers: why this is needed
- **Objectives**: what the project will achieve, **specific and measurable**: *To train 2,000 small business owners in Bandung by June 2027.* (*To improve digital literacy* is too vague: how many? who? by when?)
- **Plan** (also *Approach* or *Activities*): what you will do and how
- **Budget**: the costs, item by item, with a total
- **Timeline**: when: phases, months and deadlines (often a table)
- **Expected results** (or *Benefits*): what will change, for whom, and how you will measure it

A long proposal also starts with an **executive summary** (see the next section).

id.text:
Ulasan singkat: di B2 kamu sudah menulis surat formal dan **laporan** singkat (*Introduction, Findings, Recommendations*), dan di pelajaran sebelumnya kamu memadatkan ide ke dalam frasa kata benda (*a sharp rise in online sales*). Sekarang dokumen yang lebih besar di dunia kerja.

**Proposal** (usulan kegiatan atau proposal dana) meminta pembaca, misalnya manajer, kementerian atau donor, untuk **menyetujui dan membiayai pekerjaan di masa depan**. **Laporan** (report) menceritakan apa yang sudah terjadi atau apa yang ditemukan. Keduanya memakai **judul bagian** (heading: nama pendek di atas setiap bagian), supaya pembaca yang sibuk bisa langsung melompat ke bagian yang dia butuhkan.

Proposal biasanya punya enam judul bagian ini (tiap organisasi menamainya sedikit berbeda, dan banyak kementerian serta donor memberi template sendiri: ikuti template itu):
- **Background** (latar belakang): masalah atau peluang **saat ini**, dengan beberapa fakta dan angka: mengapa ini dibutuhkan
- **Objectives** (tujuan): apa yang akan dicapai proyek, **spesifik dan terukur**: *To train 2,000 small business owners in Bandung by June 2027.* (*To improve digital literacy* terlalu kabur: berapa orang? siapa? kapan?)
- **Plan** (rencana; juga *Approach* atau *Activities*): apa yang akan kamu lakukan dan bagaimana caranya
- **Budget** (anggaran): biaya per item, dengan totalnya
- **Timeline** (jadwal): kapan: tahap, bulan dan tenggat waktu (sering berbentuk tabel)
- **Expected results** (hasil yang diharapkan; atau *Benefits*): apa yang akan berubah, untuk siapa, dan bagaimana kamu mengukurnya

Proposal yang panjang juga diawali dengan **executive summary** (lihat bagian berikutnya).

blocks.text:
**Indonesian proposal habits to drop.** They are polite in Indonesian, just not the convention in English business writing.
1) **The long opening**: *Kata Pengantar, Puji syukur kehadirat Tuhan Yang Maha Esa …, Dengan hormat* → leave it out. Start with the purpose.
2) **A Background that starts with history**: *Indonesia adalah negara kepulauan …, Sejak zaman dahulu …, Di era globalisasi ini …* (*In this era of globalisation …*) → start with **today's** problem and a number.
3) **The campus template** (*BAB I Pendahuluan, Rumusan Masalah, Maksud dan Tujuan*) → the English headings above.
4) **The ending**: *Demikian proposal ini kami sampaikan. Atas perhatian dan kerja samanya kami ucapkan terima kasih.* → end with the next step: *We request approval by 30 November.* or *We would welcome the opportunity to discuss this proposal.*
5) **Money**: Indonesian writes *Rp1.200.000.000* and *Rp1,2 miliar*; English swaps the marks: **Rp1,200,000,000** and **Rp1.2 billion** (also written *IDR 1.2 billion*). *miliar* = **billion**, *juta* = **million**.

id.text:
**Kebiasaan proposal Indonesia yang perlu ditinggalkan.** Dalam bahasa Indonesia semua ini sopan, hanya saja bukan kebiasaan dalam tulisan bisnis berbahasa Inggris.
1) **Pembukaan yang panjang**: *Kata Pengantar, Puji syukur kehadirat Tuhan Yang Maha Esa …, Dengan hormat* → hilangkan. Mulai dengan tujuanmu.
2) **Latar belakang yang dimulai dari sejarah**: *Indonesia adalah negara kepulauan …, Sejak zaman dahulu …, Di era globalisasi ini …* (*In this era of globalisation …*) → mulai dengan masalah **hari ini** dan sebuah angka.
3) **Template kampus** (*BAB I Pendahuluan, Rumusan Masalah, Maksud dan Tujuan*) → pakai judul bagian bahasa Inggris di atas.
4) **Penutup**: *Demikian proposal ini kami sampaikan. Atas perhatian dan kerja samanya kami ucapkan terima kasih.* → akhiri dengan langkah berikutnya: *We request approval by 30 November.* atau *We would welcome the opportunity to discuss this proposal.*
5) **Uang**: bahasa Indonesia menulis *Rp1.200.000.000* dan *Rp1,2 miliar*; bahasa Inggris menukar tandanya: **Rp1,200,000,000** dan **Rp1.2 billion** (juga ditulis *IDR 1.2 billion*). *miliar* = **billion**, *juta* = **million**.

blocks.prompt: Bu Ani is rewriting the start of her Background section. Which first sentence is best for an English proposal?
options: Indonesia is an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands, and in this era of globalisation, technology is very important.
Last year, the city's small business office received more than 600 complaints about fake payment links.
First of all, we would like to thank God and everyone who has supported this proposal.
blocks.explain: The Background starts with **today's problem and a number**. The first option starts with general facts about Indonesia, and the third is a polite opening that English proposals leave out.

id.prompt: Bu Ani sedang menulis ulang awal bagian Background-nya. Kalimat pertama mana yang paling tepat untuk proposal berbahasa Inggris?
id.explain: Background dimulai dengan **masalah hari ini dan sebuah angka**. Pilihan pertama dimulai dengan fakta umum tentang Indonesia, dan pilihan ketiga adalah pembukaan sopan yang tidak dipakai di proposal berbahasa Inggris.

material.title: The executive summary: written last, read first

id.title: Executive summary: ditulis terakhir, dibaca pertama

blocks.text:
Budi works for an e-commerce company in Surabaya. The director gets his 30-page report on late deliveries, and she will read **one page**: the **executive summary** (the whole document on one page). If that page isn't clear, nothing happens.

- **Written last**: you can only summarise the findings when you know them.
- **Read first**, and often read alone: it must make sense without the rest.
- **One page or less**, for a **busy reader** who decides.

It answers four questions, in this order:
1. **Purpose**: what is this document about, or what does it ask for?
2. **Key findings**: the two or three most important facts, with numbers.
3. **Recommendations**: what should happen next.
4. **The decision needed**: what you want the reader to do, by when, and what it costs.

Put the **bottom line up front** (**BLUF**): the main point in the **first sentence**: *This report finds that … and recommends …* / *This proposal requests Rp1.2 billion to …*. An executive summary is not an introduction or a table of contents (*This report consists of five chapters* ✗), and it has no information that isn't in the document.

id.text:
Budi bekerja di sebuah perusahaan e-commerce di Surabaya. Direktur menerima laporannya tentang keterlambatan pengiriman setebal 30 halaman, dan dia hanya akan membaca **satu halaman**: **executive summary** (ringkasan eksekutif: seluruh dokumen dalam satu halaman). Kalau halaman itu tidak jelas, tidak ada yang terjadi.

- **Ditulis terakhir**: kamu baru bisa meringkas temuan setelah kamu tahu temuannya.
- **Dibaca pertama**, dan sering dibaca sendirian: harus bisa dipahami tanpa bagian lain.
- **Satu halaman atau kurang**, untuk **pembaca sibuk** yang mengambil keputusan.

Isinya menjawab empat pertanyaan, dengan urutan ini:
1. **Purpose** (tujuan): dokumen ini tentang apa, atau meminta apa?
2. **Key findings** (temuan utama): dua atau tiga fakta terpenting, dengan angka.
3. **Recommendations** (rekomendasi): apa yang sebaiknya dilakukan selanjutnya.
4. **The decision needed** (keputusan yang diminta): apa yang kamu ingin pembaca lakukan, paling lambat kapan, dan berapa biayanya.

Taruh **intinya di depan** (**BLUF**, bottom line up front): poin utama di **kalimat pertama**: *This report finds that … and recommends …* / *This proposal requests Rp1.2 billion to …*. Executive summary bukan pendahuluan atau daftar isi (*This report consists of five chapters* ✗), dan tidak berisi informasi yang tidak ada di dokumennya.

rows.en: This report finds that most late deliveries in Surabaya begin at the warehouse, and recommends three changes costing Rp450 million a year.
rows.id: Laporan ini menemukan bahwa sebagian besar keterlambatan pengiriman di Surabaya berawal di gudang, dan merekomendasikan tiga perubahan dengan biaya Rp450 juta per tahun.

id.note: tujuan dan poin utama di depan (BLUF)

rows.en: In the third quarter, 18% of orders arrived late.
rows.id: Pada kuartal ketiga, 18% pesanan tiba terlambat.
rows.note: a key finding, with a number

rows.en: Six in ten late parcels missed the 3 p.m. sorting cut-off at the Rungkut warehouse.
rows.id: Enam dari sepuluh paket yang terlambat melewati batas waktu sortir pukul 15.00 di gudang Rungkut.

rows.en: We recommend adding an evening sorting shift at the Rungkut warehouse.
rows.id: Kami merekomendasikan penambahan shift sortir malam di gudang Rungkut.

rows.en: We ask the board to approve Rp450 million by 30 November, so that the changes can start in January.
rows.id: Kami meminta direksi menyetujui Rp450 juta paling lambat 30 November, agar perubahan bisa dimulai bulan Januari.
rows.note: the decision needed: what, how much, by when

id.note: keputusan yang diminta: apa, berapa, paling lambat kapan

blocks.text: **Indonesian trap: the polite warm-up.** A *Kata Pengantar*, *Puji syukur …* or *Laporan ini disusun dalam rangka …* (*This report was prepared in the framework of …*) delays the point, and the director stops reading before she reaches it. If you want to thank people, add a short *Acknowledgements* section at the end. Open the summary with the main finding and the recommendation.

id.text: **Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: basa-basi pembuka.** *Kata Pengantar*, *Puji syukur …* atau *Laporan ini disusun dalam rangka …* (*This report was prepared in the framework of …*) menunda poin utamanya, dan direktur berhenti membaca sebelum sampai ke sana. Kalau kamu ingin berterima kasih, tambahkan bagian *Acknowledgements* yang singkat di akhir. Buka ringkasannya dengan temuan utama dan rekomendasi.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence does NOT belong in Budi's executive summary?
options: This report consists of five chapters, which are explained below.
Most late parcels missed the afternoon sorting cut-off.
We ask the board to approve the budget by 30 November.
blocks.explain: An executive summary gives the point, not a **table of contents**. A key finding and the decision needed both belong there.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang TIDAK cocok di executive summary Budi?
id.explain: Executive summary memberi poin utamanya, bukan **daftar isi**. Temuan utama dan keputusan yang diminta sama-sama cocok di sana.

blocks.text:
Recommendations are the part that leads to action, so make each one:
- **Clear**: one action per recommendation.
- **Actionable**: who does what, and by when. *Delivery should be improved* ✗ (who? how?) → *The operations team should add an evening sorting shift from 1 December.*
- **Prioritised**: numbered, the most important first.
- **Linked to the findings**: every recommendation answers a finding: *Based on Finding 2, …* (*Based on* = berdasarkan: a phrase to remember).

Useful patterns:
- **We recommend + -ing**: *We recommend adding an evening sorting shift.*
- **We recommend that + we / a plural subject + verb**: *We recommend that drivers receive a route map every morning.*
- **should + verb**: *The company should review the routes every month.*
- **It is recommended that …** (the formal phrase from B2): *It is recommended that staff use the new app.*
- In a **numbered list**, start with the plain verb: *1. Add an evening sorting shift. 2. Review the routes every month.*

In a proposal, the same idea comes at the end as the **decision needed**: *We request approval of Rp1.2 billion by 30 November.*

id.text:
Rekomendasi adalah bagian yang menghasilkan tindakan, jadi buat setiap rekomendasi:
- **Jelas**: satu tindakan per rekomendasi.
- **Bisa dijalankan** (actionable): siapa melakukan apa, dan paling lambat kapan. *Delivery should be improved* ✗ (siapa? bagaimana?) → *The operations team should add an evening sorting shift from 1 December.*
- **Berprioritas**: diberi nomor, yang paling penting di urutan pertama.
- **Terhubung dengan temuan**: setiap rekomendasi menjawab sebuah temuan: *Based on Finding 2, …* (*Based on* = berdasarkan: frasa untuk dihafal).

Pola yang berguna:
- **We recommend + -ing**: *We recommend adding an evening sorting shift.*
- **We recommend that + we / subjek jamak + kata kerja**: *We recommend that drivers receive a route map every morning.*
- **should + kata kerja**: *The company should review the routes every month.*
- **It is recommended that …** (frasa formal dari B2): *It is recommended that staff use the new app.*
- Dalam **daftar bernomor**, mulai dengan kata kerja dasar: *1. Add an evening sorting shift. 2. Review the routes every month.*

Di proposal, ide yang sama muncul di akhir sebagai **keputusan yang diminta**: *We request approval of Rp1.2 billion by 30 November.*

blocks.text:
**Indonesian trap: recommend to.** *Kami merekomendasikan untuk menambah …* → *We recommend to add …* ✗. After **recommend**, use **-ing** or **that**: *We recommend **adding** …* / *We recommend **that** we add …*. The same goes for **suggest**: *We suggest **moving** the cut-off*, not *suggest to move* ✗. (*propose* is different: *We propose to open …* and *We propose opening …* are both correct.)
Also: *rekomendasi* is the noun **recommendation**; the verb is **recommend**: *We recommendation …* ✗.

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: recommend to.** *Kami merekomendasikan untuk menambah …* → *We recommend to add …* ✗. Setelah **recommend**, pakai **-ing** atau **that**: *We recommend **adding** …* / *We recommend **that** we add …*. Sama halnya dengan **suggest**: *We suggest **moving** the cut-off*, bukan *suggest to move* ✗. (*propose* berbeda: *We propose to open …* dan *We propose opening …* sama-sama benar.)
Selain itu: *rekomendasi* adalah kata benda **recommendation**; kata kerjanya **recommend**: *We recommendation …* ✗.

blocks.prompt: Which recommendation is the easiest to act on?
options: Communication with customers should be improved.
We think that maybe the situation with customers needs more attention.
The customer service team should text every customer whose parcel is more than a day late, starting in December.
blocks.explain: It says **who** (the customer service team), **what** (text the customer), **when** (more than a day late, from December). The other two are vague: nobody knows what to do on Monday morning.

id.prompt: Rekomendasi mana yang paling mudah langsung dijalankan?
id.explain: Rekomendasi ini menyebut **siapa** (tim customer service), **apa** (mengirim SMS ke pelanggan), **kapan** (terlambat lebih dari sehari, mulai Desember). Dua lainnya kabur: tidak ada yang tahu harus berbuat apa hari Senin pagi.

blocks.text:
Business readers are busy. **Concise** writing says the same thing in fewer words, without losing meaning or politeness.

**1. Cut filler and wordy phrases.** **Filler** adds words but no meaning:
- *in order to* → **to**
- *due to the fact that* → **because**
- *at this point in time* → **now**
- *make a decision regarding* → **decide on**
- *a large number of* → **many**
- *with regard to* → **about**
- *prior to* → **before**
- *in the event that* → **if**
- *has the ability to* → **can**
- *It should be noted that …* → **delete it** and just give the fact
These are not grammar mistakes, only longer than needed. *In order to* is still useful sometimes: *in order not to miss the deadline*.

**2. Use the active when it matters who acts.** *Mistakes were made in the warehouse.* (who?) → *The night team sent 300 parcels to the wrong route.* The passive is still right when the doer is unknown or unimportant: *All parcels are scanned twice.*

**3. One idea per sentence.** Aim for about 15–25 words. Split long sentences joined with *and … which … so …*.

**4. Front-load the point** (BLUF) in emails and paragraphs too: the main point first, then the details.

**5. Don't overdo nominalisation.** From the last lesson: noun phrases are good in titles and summaries (*a 20% fall in late deliveries*), but *make a decision regarding, conduct a review of, give consideration to* hide the verb. Use the verb: **decide on, review, consider**.

id.text:
Pembaca bisnis itu sibuk. Tulisan yang **ringkas** (concise) menyampaikan hal yang sama dengan lebih sedikit kata, tanpa kehilangan makna atau kesopanan.

**1. Buang kata pengisi dan frasa bertele-tele.** **Kata pengisi** (filler) menambah kata tapi tidak menambah makna:
- *in order to* → **to**
- *due to the fact that* → **because**
- *at this point in time* → **now**
- *make a decision regarding* → **decide on**
- *a large number of* → **many**
- *with regard to* → **about**
- *prior to* → **before**
- *in the event that* → **if**
- *has the ability to* → **can**
- *It should be noted that …* → **hapus saja** dan langsung sebut faktanya
Ini bukan kesalahan tata bahasa, hanya lebih panjang dari yang perlu. *In order to* kadang tetap berguna: *in order not to miss the deadline*.

**2. Pakai kalimat aktif kalau penting siapa pelakunya.** *Mistakes were made in the warehouse.* (siapa?) → *The night team sent 300 parcels to the wrong route.* Kalimat pasif tetap tepat kalau pelakunya tidak diketahui atau tidak penting: *All parcels are scanned twice.*

**3. Satu ide per kalimat.** Usahakan sekitar 15–25 kata. Pecah kalimat panjang yang disambung dengan *and … which … so …*.

**4. Taruh poinnya di depan** (BLUF) di email dan paragraf juga: poin utama dulu, baru detailnya.

**5. Jangan berlebihan dengan nominalisasi.** Dari pelajaran sebelumnya: frasa kata benda bagus untuk judul dan ringkasan (*a 20% fall in late deliveries*), tapi *make a decision regarding, conduct a review of, give consideration to* menyembunyikan kata kerjanya. Pakai kata kerjanya: **decide on, review, consider**.

rows.id: Agar dapat mengambil keputusan mengenai masalah anggaran, … → Untuk memutuskan anggaran, …

id.note: prior to → before; a large number of → many

blocks.text:
**Indonesian trap: the very long sentence.** Indonesian formal writing often joins many ideas with *yang, dan, sehingga, serta, dalam rangka*. Translated word for word, one sentence becomes 60 words long and the reader gets lost: split it. Watch for word-for-word fillers too: *dalam rangka* → *in the framework of* ✗ → **to** / **for**; *terkait dengan hal tersebut* → *related to that matter* → **about this**; *perlu diketahui bahwa* → *it needs to be known that* → delete it.
And concise is not telegraphic: *Hire drivers. Fix routes.* is fine in your own notes, but in a report keep full, polite sentences.

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: kalimat yang sangat panjang.** Tulisan formal bahasa Indonesia sering menyambung banyak ide dengan *yang, dan, sehingga, serta, dalam rangka*. Kalau diterjemahkan kata per kata, satu kalimat jadi 60 kata dan pembaca tersesat: pecah kalimatnya. Waspadai juga kata pengisi hasil terjemahan kata per kata: *dalam rangka* → *in the framework of* ✗ → **to** / **for**; *terkait dengan hal tersebut* → *related to that matter* → **about this**; *perlu diketahui bahwa* → *it needs to be known that* → hapus saja.
Dan ringkas bukan berarti seperti telegram: *Hire drivers. Fix routes.* boleh di catatanmu sendiri, tapi di laporan tetap pakai kalimat lengkap dan sopan.

blocks.prompt: Which is the best concise version of: 'With regard to the new app, a large number of drivers have said that it has the ability to save time.'
options: Many drivers say the new app can save time.
Regarding the new app, a large number of drivers have said it has the ability to save time.
New app: saves time, drivers say.
blocks.explain: **with regard to** goes, **a large number of → many**, **has the ability to → can**: same meaning, half the words. The second option keeps most of the filler; the third is so short that it isn't a full sentence.

id.prompt: Mana versi ringkas yang paling tepat dari: 'With regard to the new app, a large number of drivers have said that it has the ability to save time.'
id.explain: **with regard to** dibuang, **a large number of → many**, **has the ability to → can**: maknanya sama, katanya separuh. Pilihan kedua masih menyimpan sebagian besar kata pengisinya; pilihan ketiga terlalu pendek sampai bukan kalimat lengkap lagi.

id.intro: Direktur atau kementerian tidak akan membaca 40 halaman: mereka membaca halaman pertama lalu memutuskan. Di pelajaran ini kamu menyusun proposal dengan judul bagian yang jelas, menulis executive summary dan rekomendasi yang bisa langsung ditindaklanjuti pembaca yang sibuk, dan membuang kata pengisi yang membuat tulisan bisnis berbahasa Inggris panjang dan berat.

assessment.pw-1: Proposal Bu Ani untuk kementerian punya enam judul bagian: Background, Objectives, Plan, Budget, Timeline, Expected results. Di bawah judul bagian mana baris-baris ini? Tulis judul bagiannya. 'Trainer recruitment: November–December 2026. Workshops: January–June 2027. Final evaluation: by the end of September 2027.'
assessment.pw-2: Proposal yang sama, enam judul bagian yang sama: Background, Objectives, Plan, Budget, Timeline, Expected results. Di bawah judul bagian mana kalimat ini? Tulis judul bagiannya. 'Each three-hour workshop will have three parts: setting up QRIS, spotting fake payment links, and practice on the participants' own phones.'
assessment.pw-3: Executive summary Budi untuk direktur punya empat bagian: Purpose, Key findings, Recommendations, Decision needed. Kalimat ini termasuk bagian yang mana? Tulis namanya. 'Seven in ten complaints in the third quarter came from customers who did not know where their parcel was.'
assessment.pw-4: Lengkapi rekomendasi Budi dengan satu kata kerja bahasa Inggris: 'Based on Finding 3, we ___ sending customers an automatic WhatsApp message when a parcel is late.'
assessment.pw-5: Buat kalimat dari laporan Budi ini lebih ringkas: ganti 'due to the fact that' dengan satu kata bahasa Inggris. 'Many drivers missed their delivery slots due to the fact that the road to the warehouse was flooded.'
assessment.pw-6: Buat kalimat ini lebih ringkas: ganti 'make a decision regarding' dengan dua kata bahasa Inggris. 'The board will make a decision regarding the new warehouse on Friday.'
assessment.pw-7: Buang frasa pengisinya dan tulis seluruh kalimatnya dalam bahasa Inggris secara ringkas: 'It should be noted that complaints about late parcels fell sharply in October.'
